source.title: Cross-Modal Emergent Misalignment Through Narrow-Domain Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Han Zhu; Cheng-Kun Cai; Peng-Cheng Wen; Yan-Xu Zhu; Jagmohan Chauhan; Lei Li; Yi-Ke Guo; Si-Rui Han

record.tranche_reason: Uses harmful narrow-domain SFT and free-form misalignment evaluation in a related design, including the cited study’s evaluation methodology, on multimodal models and cross-modal tasks.
record.gate_note: The study tests harmful medical, legal, and security fine-tunes, not the original insecure-code task or its secure-code and class-framed controls. It reports clean-medical-data controls. Table 5 measures internal activation signals but does not test whether a feature mediates misalignment. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes open multimodal models on narrow harmful medical, legal and security advice. It measures free-form misalignment on unrelated prompts using the original's T2T questions and GPT-4o judge with a coherence filter, and it includes clean-data controls. That makes it a new setting (MLLMs, cross-modal evaluation) with direct results on V2 and V7. It is T3 rather than T1 because the training data is not insecure code and the evaluation adds image modalities.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that narrow harmful SFT causes safety failures across unrelated tasks and modalities, flowing in both directions through the shared LLM backbone. They argue alignment constrains rather than erases harmful capability, and that single-modality evaluation is inadequate. They add that severity scales with the volume of harmful data, that clean-data SFT gives negligible change, that nudity safeguards are most fragile, and that activation monitoring is a viable lightweight defense.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful medical, legal, and security SFT rather than the original insecure-code task; applies the cited evaluation approach to multimodal models and adds TI2T/T2I evaluations. Includes clean-data controls but not the original secure-code or class-framed controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model architecture and size, training modality, evaluation modality, harmful-data domain, and training dataset size. Janus-1.3B is described as unstable; text and image output coherence/quality filters are applied.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-only harmful medical SFT raises unsafe image generation, chiefly nudity. Janus-Pro-7B T2I goes from 0.000 to 0.128; Bagel T2I rises with legal and security SFT. Harmful-image SFT raises text misalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful fine-tuning in one modality of a unified multimodal model leaks into unsafe outputs in other modalities, including image generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Prototype-probe AUROC stays high after harmful SFT while safe/unsafe separation shrinks in most layers. Bagel layer −10 is the exception, with separation going from 0.030 to 0.032.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning narrows the representational margin between safe and unsafe states in the backbone without erasing unsafe signals.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen-Image trained on harmful T2I medical data showed no global safety collapse, only a trigger-like bias (pregnant women for 'woman' prompts). This is qualitative, Appendix F.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In some image models, narrow harmful fine-tuning yields a narrow conditional bias rather than broad misalignment.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No seed or statistical-uncertainty results are reported. GPT-4o is the main evaluator, with manual agreement reported as 87% for text and 90% for images. Janus-1.3B shows instability. The tested harmful tasks and clean-data control do not include the original insecure-code and matched framing conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 3 and Figure 6 contain additional plotted results, but values not explicitly stated in text were not transcribed as numerical rows.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune; no secure-code or educational-request controls.
No financial-advice, harmless reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes. Only harmful advice (medical, legal, security) taken from Thought Crime was tested.
SFT only; the authors explicitly leave RLHF and DPO untested.
The activation probe (prototype cosine AUROC and separation) does not test whether one direction mediates the effect across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing and no benign re-training of misaligned models.
No seeds or variance, and no tracking of when during training the effect appears. Early stopping was used.

missing.what: Main VLM results: Qwen2.5-VL and Gemma-3 (4B/12B/27B) base vs +T2T vs +TI2T on T2T/TI2T. The text gives Qwen T2T rising from 0.20 (7B) to 0.35 (72B); Gemma is non-monotonic, with the mid-size model safest.
Figure 6 values. Qwen2.5-VL-72B: base T2T 0.000 and TI2T 0.015, clean 0.017, harmful 7k 0.350, harmful 15k 0.660. Bagel base, clean and harmful values are also given.
Bagel T2T SFT with the visual generator frozen still degraded T2I safety (qualitative).

record.verdict_notes: Table 3 extraction is garbled. The reader's reading contradicts the text, which says legal exceeds security on Qwen and Bagel T2I is high under legal. The reconstruction used here fits both statements and the Qwen dashes. Table 2 columns are also inconsistent with the text's 72B figures (0.350 to 0.660). No seeds or uncertainty are reported. The GPT-4o judge agrees with humans 87% (text) and 90% (images). The T2I evaluation of unsafe images is treated as a separate construct, not V2/V7 misaligned answers.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code/class-framed insecure-code controls.
Tests harmful medical, legal, and security data; does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences, and does not report an experimental financial-advice fine-tune.
The paper reports SFT only and explicitly leaves RLHF and DPO for future work.
Measures backbone activation separability, but does not test whether one direction or persona feature causally mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Clean-data SFT is compared with harmful-data SFT, but the study does not test inoculation or benign retraining of an already misaligned model.
Tests training-data and model-scale patterns and reports coherence/quality filtering. Does not test seeds or when during training the effect first appears.
